title: Teaching CLIP to Count to Ten
why_added: trains a counting-aware CLIP; named by Counting Guidance, p. 9
reads: Final CLIP or BASIC embeddings of a clean image, its true caption and the caption with the number word swapped; no noisy image or latent reaches the counting model
trained_on: Finetunes pretrained CLIP/BASIC for 20K steps on web data plus a detector-verified counting set (about 37K each for two to six, 1.5K to 7K for seven to ten) with L = L_CLIP + 1 * L_count, a one-word counterfactual caption contrast
gradient_enters: No classifier gradient enters the sampler; the finetuned CLIP-L/14 enters a newly trained Imagen model through the text encoder, sampled with DDPM, and Eq. 2's gradient updates CLIP weights only during finetuning
unseen: no; CountBench holds out images from the training set, but no object categories are held out or compared
headline: Count accuracy on CountBench (540 clean images, 9 count choices, higher is better) 75.93% against 32.94% best baseline for CLIP-B/32 (31.67% official); at count two 97% against 78% for public CLIP-L/14
copy_or_avoid: Copy the one-word hard negative and detector-verified labels; avoid reading its 97% at count two as evidence for two different subjects or noisy inputs, since it counts one kind on clean images (inferred)
model: CLIP-B/32 / CLIP-L/14 / BASIC-S; Imagen for generation
